solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Proper advices on breaking up

indicators.note: something breaking up falls to pieces, so the letters before it are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the thirteen letters of the two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A columnist offering sound counsel to couples who are splitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the two opening words rearrange to DIVORCE PAPERS, and the clue read straight describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal documents filed to end a marriage are the formal notices served when a couple separates.

clue.text: Female duck makes such a noise!

indicators.note: the noise a word makes is its sound, so the bird's name is taken as spoken

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck; in a non-rhotic accent its name is said like the girl's name

explanation.surface: A joke about a hen duck quacking loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: The eider, a large sea duck, is pronounced EYE-duh in British speech, with no final R sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a traditional girl's name, so a woman could be called it; the definition is a loose example.

clue.text: Invisible to us, this new blue-green: no chrome at first nor ultimately seen

definitions.text: Invisible to us, this new blue-green

indicators.note: no says the following piece is not wanted and must come out of the word
nor continues the refusal, so a second piece must also come out

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue itself is named as a word

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter, which is removed

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter only of the word after it

parts.note: the closing letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: A report on a newly discovered colour that the human eye cannot normally perceive.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon after 'blue-green' is part of the wordplay: take COLON and lose its C and N. Olo was announced in 2025 by researchers who stimulated single cone cells with lasers.
explanation.definitionFit: Olo is the name scientists gave to a saturated blue-green hue that only appears when retinal cones are stimulated directly.

clue.text: About face: the struggles consuming a spiritual office

parts.note: circa, abbreviated, means about

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the rearranged letters swallow the next piece
struggles suggests writhing about, so the letters of the preceding word are thrown into a new order

parts.note: face as in cheek or insolence
taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, swallowed by the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Turning around to face the difficulties that take over a religious post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About face' reads as the military command, but the two words are separate pieces; face here means cheek or insolence.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliphate is the office or reign of a caliph, the religious and political successor to Muhammad.

clue.text: To secure sweetfish, two pennies satisfy vendor

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the pair of letters grips the fish between them

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny, twice
the ayu is a small East Asian fish also called sweetfish

explanation.surface: Paying a fishmonger a couple of coins to get some sweetfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The ayu is a Japanese river fish known as sweetfish for its flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay up is to hand over the money owed, which is what keeps a seller content.

clue.text: Before set piece by Sterling, even score penalty

indicators.note: before places the last-named item ahead of the pieces named first, setting the running order

parts.note: par is level or an even score, as in golf
a piece in a chess set
sterling means of fine quality

explanation.surface: A football match report: a level score before a set piece taken by a player called Sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set piece' and 'Sterling' call up football and Raheem Sterling; they are a chess piece and an adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking fine is a monetary penalty charged for leaving a vehicle where it is not permitted.

clue.text: Catch Johnny almost in mid air after launch, torn to pieces

indicators.note: a launched rocket rises, and in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: to catch is to trap

indicators.note: a three-letter word has no exact centre, so the actor goes in nearly at its midpoint

parts.note: taken as written, opened after its first letter
the actor Johnny Depp

explanation.surface: A fielder taking a catch in mid-air just after the ball is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAP then A(DEPP)IR is read upwards in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripped apart describes something pulled violently into fragments, a past participle matching torn to pieces.

clue.text: Memorial for best friend wild pig ate, scoffing heel in soup

indicators.note: scoffing means wolfing down food, so the rearranged letters swallow what follows
in places the contemptible person inside the bowl of food
wild means out of control, so the letters that follow run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup
a heel and a toad are both a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A dog's tribute after a wild pig gobbled a heel of bread in its soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Epitaph to a Dog is Byron's poem for his Newfoundland, Boatswain; 'best friend' is the dog, as in man's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron wrote the poem as a tombstone inscription for his dog, so it is literally a memorial verse for a beloved pet.

clue.text: Gain an advantage over child to keep rapper in school

indicators.note: to keep is to hold inside, so the first piece wraps round the rest

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: in places the performer inside the verb for instruction

parts.note: to school someone is to teach them
Kendrick Lamar, the American rapper

explanation.surface: A child keeping a rap star in school seems to gain the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: SON holds TEACH, which holds LAMAR: S(TEA(LAMAR)CH)ON. 'School' is a verb here, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal a march on someone is an idiom for getting ahead of them by acting first.

clue.text: Rubbish work in theatre restricts independent film musician

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the first pieces enclose the letter for independent

parts.note: to pan a show is to rubbish it
an op is an operation, work done in an operating theatre
I is the abbreviation for independent
a film is a thin layer

explanation.surface: A critic trashing a stage show that kept an indie film musician in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the operating theatre, where surgeons work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist, someone who plays the piano, is a kind of musician; the definition is a broader category.

clue.text: Spot on some butter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small portion of butter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a stain on butter; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat means apt or exactly timed as an adjective, and a small shaped piece of butter as a noun.

clue.text: What identifies playground game?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a label attached to identify something
second meaning: the chasing game where one child touches another

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it look like a quiz about naming a game; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a label used for identification, and also the children's chase game known as tig or it.

clue.text: Part of school melody Dame Judi's inscribed in seat out back?

indicators.note: something inscribed in is written inside, so the actress's surname sits within the other pieces

parts.note: a gar is a fish, one member of a school
the actress Dame Judi Dench
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A school song with Judi Dench's name carved into a bench at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests pupils, but it is a school of fish. 'Out back' means in the back garden, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden chair is outdoor furniture, the kind of seat found in a back yard.

clue.text: One-pic flicks entertaining youngster and mum?

definitions.text: One-pic flicks entertaining youngster and mum?

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
to flick is to toss with a quick movement, so the letters before it are flung into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a pup is a young person, informally
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A one-film showing laid on for a child and mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flicks' looks like a noun for films but works as a verb; read whole, the clue describes a temporary screening that families drop into.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up cinema is a temporary screening venue, often showing a single film to a casual audience such as parents with children.

clue.text: Take supervising function in online business? Sweet

indicators.note: supervising means standing over, so in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the take is the profit
a role, with E- for electronic as in e-commerce

explanation.surface: A manager wondering whether to take on an oversight job in an internet company.
explanation.walkthrough: E- is the prefix for electronic or online, as in email.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiterole is a small cream-filled choux bun, a classic dessert or sweet.

clue.text: Immediately a ballad singer accepts a reject

parts.note: per means a, as in so much a day

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the song holds the word for immediately

parts.note: a ballad is a song
anon is an old word for immediately
a singer is an informer, who rats
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ballad singer at once takes on a song that was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks musical, but to sing is slang for informing, and an informer is a rat. PER SO(ANON)NG RAT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona non grata is a person who is unwelcome or rejected, so it serves as a noun for a reject.

clue.text: A person insures against overlapping surveys

indicators.note: overlapping means the two words lie across each other, so one breaks into the other

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should know
to cover is to insure against

explanation.surface: Someone taking out insurance against the risk of overlapping cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlapping' tells you the two words interleave rather than sit side by side, so only one letter of the second crosses into the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Once-overs are quick inspections, so they are cursory surveys of something.

clue.text: Top dog Heald a bit worried about news letter

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the news and the Greek letter
worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
gen is slang for information
chi is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A boss called Heald fretting a little over a newsletter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News letter' reads as one thing but is two pieces: GEN and CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: The big enchilada is American slang for the most important person, the boss or top dog.

clue.text: Cuckoo perhaps heads through turbulent sea

definitions.note: an adjective; the answer completes 'to have ...'

indicators.note: through means passing within, so one piece sits inside the other
turbulent water is churned up, so the letters of the next word are stirred

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
on a ship the heads are lavatories, for example ones used by the crew

explanation.surface: A cuckoo flying headlong across a stormy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' is naval slang for toilets; 'perhaps' signals that crew loos are just one example. 'Cuckoo' is not the bird but slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a screw loose is a bit crazy, which is what cuckoo means in slang.

clue.text: Cunning exposed location within Greater Manchester

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters come off

parts.note: sleight is cunning or dexterity, as in sleight of hand

explanation.surface: A sly scheme uncovered somewhere in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Leigh is a town near Wigan in Greater Manchester, the metropolitan county around the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leigh is a market town in the Wigan borough, one of the places within that English county.

clue.text: Eye feature of climate change

indicators.note: a feature of something is part of it, so the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The eye of a storm as a characteristic of a warming climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' suggests a storm's eye, but it is a private eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Tec is short for detective, and a private eye is a detective.

clue.text: Eggs done as instructed?

indicators.note: an instruction is delivered by voice, so the word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: over means done or finished, said without the final R

explanation.surface: Eggs cooked exactly following the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done' suggests cooked eggs, but it means finished. In British speech the word sounds like OVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural of ovum, the biological term for egg cells.

clue.text: Wee instrument's dropped by Hardy, say, Nelson's predecessor

parts.note: Oliver Hardy, of Laurel and Hardy; 'say' marks him as one example of an Oliver

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: a hand-held percussion instrument
wee is urine; this is removed

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy, or perhaps Nelson's captain, dropping a little instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' and 'Nelson' suggest Trafalgar, but Nelson is Nelson Mandela, and 'Wee' is not small.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Tambo led the ANC before Nelson Mandela became its president in 1991.

clue.text: Character doing up university

indicators.note: in a down answer up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned round

parts.note: at means doing, as in what are you at?
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone renovating a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing up' looks like decorating, but 'up' turns AT round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: The fifth PM

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fifth month of the year
second meaning: Theresa ..., British prime minister 2016 to 2019

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the fifth prime minister in some list; the halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the fifth month of the calendar and the surname of a former Conservative prime minister.

clue.text: Gear saving lives reportedly breaks young men

definitions.note: the answer is plural; the gear is a set of rescue devices

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: breaches are breaks
boys are young men

explanation.surface: News that safety equipment has failed some young men.
explanation.walkthrough: A breeches buoy is a lifebuoy with canvas shorts attached, slung on a rope to haul people from a wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeches buoys are sea-rescue apparatus used to pull people to safety along a line, so they are life-saving gear.
